# Explore Workbench, Phase 4: Workflows (Escape order, selection bar and undo, filter panel, search feedback, notifications, loading/empty/drop, import/export menus, figure editor, structure picker, display-name text) — Implementation Plan

<!-- Code snippets keep the indentation of the files they edit, so Prettier leaves this plan as written. -->
<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make the everyday tasks on `/explore` say what happened and allow a way back (design decisions 11, 13, 14, 15). Escape takes one step per press through one order (the top layer, then the EAT connectors, then the selection, then the tool). A selection bar on the plot offers "Show only these · Zoom to them · Copy IDs · Clear", and chips in the plot's bottom-left corner say when the view is filtered, isolated or has hidden categories. ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z undoes selection changes, "show only" steps and filter apply or reset. The query builder becomes the sidebar's Filter panel, with a draft that applies only on Apply, a live count and a stated reason when Apply is disabled. Search reports found and missing IDs and zooms to a single hit. Notifications share one style with a close button and up to two actions, Reset filters offers Undo, and clearing stored data asks first. The loading overlay tells the truth, an empty plot invites a drop, and a file dragged anywhere over the workbench can be dropped. The Import menu doubles as the dataset switcher and remembers the last file; the Export menu lists its five exports and every export confirms. The figure editor becomes a full-screen `ps-dialog` (Escape, Close, Undo inside it) and is split under 800 lines. The structure header lets the user pick which selected protein shows, and its links stay reachable at every width. Annotation display names and plural-aware counts reach every text site, and the annotation picker takes the kit look with the predicted-annotation icon.

**Architecture:** Behaviour stays split the way phases 2 and 3 left it: core Lit elements own their own UI and events; plain-TypeScript controllers in `apps/web/src/explore/` wire them by id; the React shell (`apps/web/src/workbench/`) owns layout and reads runtime facts only through `workbench-status.ts` and `layout-state.ts`. New plot UI (the selection bar, the status corner) are core elements rendered once by `PlotArea.tsx` and fed by controllers, so the scatterplot and `PlotArea` never re-render at brush rate. The undo history is a pure module whose instance the interaction controller owns; the selection and filter controllers record and apply their own entries, and a small undo controller owns the keys. Escape stays owned by `kit/layers.ts`: every open overlay is a layer, and the app's fallbacks (connectors, selection, tool) run in the window's bubble phase only when no component already handled the press. The figure editor, the import menu and the info popover move onto the kit's top-layer `ps-dialog` and `ps-popover`; nothing new uses `position: fixed` inside a shadow root.

**Tech Stack:** Lit 3 (legacy decorators), TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Vitest 4.1.9 (core: jsdom `unit` and Chromium `browser` projects; utils and app: node), Playwright 1.61, React 19, Sonner 2 (`sonner@^2.0.7`), the phase 1 kit (`ps-*`, `kit/layers.ts`, `@floating-ui/dom`), Lucide 0.462 (`lucide` in core, `lucide-react` in the shell), d3-zoom (the plot's transform), `Intl.NumberFormat` and `Intl.PluralRules`.

**Spec:** `openspec/changes/explore-workbench/design.md`: decisions 11 (one layer stack for Escape and closing), 13 (selection, status and undo), 14 (filter in the sidebar), 15 (search, messages, import and export, figure editor, structure, text), plus 2 (structure placements and the rail), 8 (kit building blocks), 12 (predicted icon, display names), 18 (code structure, files of about 800 lines) and 20 (testing). `proposal.md` for scope (capabilities `selection-workflow`, `explore-import-export`, `query-builder-filtering`, `query-builder-controls`, `protein-search-feedback`, `annotation-presentation`, `eat-reliability-filter`, `eat-provenance-connectors`, `example-datasets`, `support-contact`, `prep-failure-routing`, `e2e-validation`, `protein-resource-links`). `tasks.md` section 4, rewritten to this plan's sixteen tasks in the commit that adds the plan. The research notes `.superpowers/research/phase-4/R1`–`R5` map the current code with file:line; the user adopted every recommended answer in them, and where one conflicts with design.md, design.md wins (see Rulings). ## Global Constraints

From phases 1–3, unchanged:

- Every design token is a CSS custom property named `--ps-*`, declared only in `packages/core/src/styles/theme.ts`.
- New core stylesheets hold no raw colours (`#…`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, `white`, `black`) and no literal font sizes; they read `--ps-*` tokens. Size literals such as `360px` for widths are fine.
- New code never declares tokens on `:host`; tokens come from `:root`.
- `css` literals live only in `*.styles.ts` files or `styles/` folders (ESLint rule in `eslint.config.mjs`; `styles-integrity.test.ts` finds them by glob). Non-style modules must not live in `packages/core/src/styles/`, because the integrity test treats every export there as a stylesheet.
- Kit elements use the `ps-` tag prefix; feature elements keep `protspace-`.
- Icons come from Lucide only, at stroke width 1.75 and sizes 14, 16 or 20 px.
- Popovers use `popover="manual"`; dialogs use `<dialog>.showModal()`. Both render in the top layer.
- Fonts are self-hosted; never load a third-party font CDN.
- Target browsers: the last two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.
- Light accent values: fill `#007ab5` under white text, hover `#00699c`, accent text `#0369a1`, focus ring `#0284c7`. Dark: fill `#38bdf8` under `#04121c` text, hover `#7dd3fc`, accent text `#38bdf8`, focus `#38bdf8`.
- Every new export needs a consumer in the same commit (knip runs in the pre-commit hook); the task's own test file importing it is enough. Public kit API is exported from `packages/core/src/components/kit/index.ts`, which `packages/core/src/index.ts` re-exports. Exported types with no importer fail knip: keep option and view-model types module-private unless a consumer imports them.
- Commits: Angular `type(scope): subject` (`feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `chore`), subject under 72 characters, at most two lines, never a `Co-Authored-By` or Claude trailer. Commit when the task's tests pass. The husky hook runs `pnpm precommit` (lint-staged, type-check, knip, docs checks, docs build); never bypass it on a task's final commit. Type-coupled changes land in one commit.
- Run core tests package-scoped: `pnpm --filter @protspace/core exec vitest --run --project unit <file>` or `--project browser <file>`.
- Dev and e2e servers use ports other than 8080 and 8091 (the user's). For e2e set `PLAYWRIGHT_PORT`, e.g. `PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=8475 pnpm test:e2e <spec>`.
- `--ps-text-faint` is for disabled text and decorative icons only; readable secondary text, hints, placeholders, keycaps and group labels use `--ps-text-muted`.
- Runtime elements are rendered by React exactly once, unconditionally, with stable ids, never keyed or moved; a parent may re-render, but never with a `key`, a conditional or a second tree around a runtime element. The ids `#myPlot` and `#progressive-loading` and the `data-driver-id` values `scatterplot`, `legend`, `other-row`, `import`, `projections`, `search`, `selection`, `data-actions` and `help` are kept for the tour, the e2e and the perf suites. `#myDataLoader` stays mounted, hidden.
- React → runtime goes through the layout store or DOM events on elements the runtime wires by id; a React component may also call a public method of a core element it finds by id (Task 4.10's `toggleFrom`), but never reads runtime state off an element. Runtime → React goes through `workbench-status.ts` or `layout-state.ts`. React sets kit properties through props and listens to `ps-*` events with a ref and `addEventListener`.
- At rest no ancestor of the projection details card, the query builder's pickers (in the Filter panel from Task 4.5) or the import menu (until Task 4.10) gets `transform`, `translate`, `filter`, `contain` or `container-type`, and `#wb-sidebar` gets no z-index: those still use `position: fixed` inside their shadow roots. Shell z-indices are literals in `workbench.css` below the loading overlay's 9999; no z-index tokens.
- One plot resize per layout change; switching the sidebar between Legend and Filter, opening the selection bar, the status chips, toasts, the empty state and the drop area never change `#myPlot`'s box. The plot never animates: every programmatic zoom in this phase is untweened (`PlotInteractionController.setTransform`), except the existing `resetZoom()`.
- Layout persists only under `protspace:layout:v1`, parsed per field (a missing field takes its default, so the key stays v1); layout never goes into the URL. Stored legend settings, `protspace_publishState` and the OPFS `protspace-last-import` directory keep their keys and formats.
- The legend's public surface, DOM contract and persistence stay as phase 3 left them (`docs/developers/api/index.md`); this phase adds only `showAllCategories()` (Task 4.3). The legend adds no window listener and registers no Escape fallback.
- E2E: new specs are `apps/web/tests/workbench-*.spec.ts` (project `workbench`: Desktop Chrome, 1280×720, `testMatch` `workbench-*.spec.ts`). Specs reach controls through helpers (`apps/web/tests/helpers/explore.ts`, `helpers/workbench.ts`, `helpers/legend.ts`) that find them by role, accessible name or tag; a helper never uses `shadowRoot` inside `page.evaluate`. Every exported helper is used by a spec in the same commit (knip). Assert placement and state, not 3D pixels.
- Docs: the developer docs (`docs/developers/`) change in the commit that changes the public API or the architecture they describe (a removed event, property or element is a **BREAKING** note for embedders; `@protspace/core` is unpublished). The user guide (`docs/explore/`) and its images wait for phase 7, except a statement that would become false about a control this phase removes (the docs build must stay green either way).
- `pnpm docs:images` stays broken at runtime until phase 7; `pnpm type-check:scripts` (in the hook) must stay green: when a task moves a module that `scripts/docs-screenshots/*.ts` imports, it updates that import path.

- `customElement` comes from `../../utils/safe-custom-element` (relative to a component folder), never from `lit/decorators.js`. Feature elements import kit modules by file (`import '../kit/menu'`, `import { icon } from '../kit/icon'`), not the kit barrel.
- `kit/layers.ts`: `pushLayer({ close, elements, dismissOnOutsidePress? }): () => void` (the release function is safe to call twice; owners call it on close and on disconnect; include the anchor in `elements`), `topLayer()`, `onEscapeFallback(order, handle): () => void`, `ESCAPE_ORDER`. Layer Escape and outside presses are window-capture listeners. The app imports these from `@protspace/core` (one shared kit chunk, so one stack); never a second copy.
- `ps-menu` (`anchor`, `open`, `placement`, `label`, `searchable`, `search-placeholder`): the owner receives `ps-close` before `ps-select` (`detail: { value, checked }`); a radio or plain item closes the menu and hands focus back to its anchor first, a checkbox item keeps it open; Tab closes it; it sets `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded` on its anchor (do not bind them yourself); grouped items go in `ps-menu-group` (`label`); radio exclusivity is menu-wide; checked rows are tinted; the search filters items by `textContent`.
- `ps-popover` (`.anchor`, `open`, `placement`, `panel-role`, `panel-label`; events `ps-open`, `ps-close`, bubbling and composed; `dismiss()`): Escape and an outside press (press and release both outside; the anchor counts as inside) close it and fire `ps-close`; it returns focus to what was focused at open when focus was inside, never moves focus in on open, re-shows after a DOM move, caps its height with Floating UI's `size`. A nested overlay's `ps-close` stops at the outer overlay's slot wrapper, so an owner listens on the nested element itself. It does not set `aria-haspopup`/`aria-expanded` on its anchor: the owner does. Its panel keeps `translate: 0 0` at rest, which makes it a containing block for `position: fixed` children.
- `ps-dialog` (`open`, `heading`, `size` sm/md/lg/full, `dismissible`; `dismiss()`; slots default, `header-actions`, `footer`; event `ps-close`): pushes a layer while open, so Escape always closes it; `dismissible` governs only a backdrop press (`dismissible="false"` in markup means false); it renders its own close button "Close" and returns focus to the control focused or last pressed at open. `size="full"` is `calc(100vw - 32px) × calc(100dvh - 32px)`.
- `ps-button` (`variant` primary/secondary/ghost/danger, `size` sm/md; slotted text is its name; slot `start`) and `ps-icon-button` (`icon`, `label`, `pressed`, `size`, `tooltip-placement`) forward `hasPopup` and `expanded` to their inner button and take a `describedBy` element list. `ps-tooltip` (`text`, `.anchor`, `placement`, `names-target`, `show()`, `hide()`) hides on Escape and on a press of its target. `ps-input` (`value`, `type` text/search/number, `label`, `placeholder`, `invalid`, `disabled`; no `min`/`max`). `ps-select` (`.options`, `value`, `label`, `disabled`, `describedBy`; `change`). `ps-switch`, `ps-checkbox` (`checked`, `label`, `disabled`; `change`).
- Add a Lucide icon to core by importing its PascalCase export from `lucide` and adding a kebab-case key to `ICONS` in `packages/core/src/components/kit/icon.ts`, in the commit that first uses it. Keys present: `arrow-down-*`, `arrow-up-down`, `box`, `check`, `chevron-down`, `circle-help`, `download`, `ellipsis`, `eye`, `eye-off`, `grip-vertical`, `info`, `lasso`, `list`, `maximize`, `minus`, `mouse-pointer`, `panel-right`, `panel-right-close`, `panel-right-open`, `search`, `sliders-horizontal`, `sparkles`, `square-dashed`, `square-pen`, `target`, `upload`, `x` (plus any 3.14/3.15 add). This phase adds `filter` (4.3), `copy` (4.7), `external-link` (4.9), `undo-2` (4.14) when first used; a later task that uses a key confirms it is there and never adds it again. The React shell uses `lucide-react` with `strokeWidth={1.75}`.

Phase 4:

- **Escape order.** From Task 4.1: `ESCAPE_ORDER = { connectors: 10, selection: 20, tool: 30 }`. The top open layer closes in the window capture phase as today. Fallbacks run from a separate **window bubble-phase** `keydown` listener, only when no layer is open and `event.defaultPrevented` is false, in ascending order, the first that returns true wins (it calls `preventDefault`). Any component that acts on Escape without being a layer must call `preventDefault()` (`handleDropdownEscape` already does), so one press takes exactly one step. The scatterplot registers the connectors fallback itself (embedders keep it); the app registers `selection` and `tool`. The duplicate-stack spider, the pinned projection details card and the figure editor are layers.
- **Undo.** Mod+Z (⌘ on Apple platforms via `isMacOrIos()`, Ctrl elsewhere) undoes and Shift+Mod+Z redoes, heard on `document` in the bubble phase, ignored when `altKey`, `isComposing`, an editable element (`INPUT`, `TEXTAREA`, `SELECT`, contentEditable) is in the composed path, or an open modal (`<dialog open>` or `aria-modal="true"`) is in the path or open on the page; `preventDefault` only when a step was undone or redone. History: linear, `record` clears redo, at most 100 entries and 2,000,000 ids in total (the oldest drop first), entries hold the arrays callers already own (never `[...ids]`), cleared on a new dataset. Recorded: selection commits (any source, Escape included), isolate ("Show only these"), reset isolation (the chip's ✕), filter Apply, Reset and chip ✕. Not recorded: the EAT reliability slider, legend hide/show, zoom.
- **Plot UI sizes.** Selection bar: bottom-centre of the plot (`position: absolute; bottom: var(--ps-space-3); left: 50%; translate: -50% 0`), `--ps-surface-raised`, `1px solid var(--ps-border)`, `--ps-radius-lg`, `--ps-shadow-md`, padding `var(--ps-space-1)`, gap `var(--ps-space-1)`, `ps-button size="sm"` (28 px), so 38 px tall with its border. Status corner: bottom-left (`left: var(--ps-space-3); bottom: var(--ps-space-3)`), count as plain `--ps-text-sm` `--ps-text-muted` tabular text, chips 24 px tall, `inline-flex`, gap `var(--ps-space-1-5)`, padding `0 var(--ps-space-1-5) 0 var(--ps-space-2)`, `--ps-radius-full`, `--ps-accent-tint` / `--ps-accent-text`, `--ps-weight-medium`, `--ps-text-sm`, a 14 px leading icon and a trailing `ps-icon-button size="sm"` ✕ (mockup `palette.html:115`). The EAT `.connector-status` moves from bottom-centre to top-centre (`top: var(--ps-space-2)`). The plot's bottom-right corner stays free (the EAT e2e clicks there).
- **Notifications.** One workbench toaster (`<Toaster id="workbench">`), bottom-centre of the plot area, at most 3 visible, toast width at most 360 px, `--offset-bottom` 12 px, raised by the selection bar's height plus 12 px while the bar shows (CSS `:has(#mySelectionBar:not([hidden]))`), every toast with a close button named "Dismiss notification", colours from tokens, `theme="light"` (tokens follow `data-theme` in phase 6). Durations stay 4/5/8/10 s (success/info/warning/error); an Undo toast lasts 8 s. Toasts raised while a modal dialog is open are hidden under the top layer, so the figure editor shows its own feedback inside the dialog (Task 4.14).
- **Counts and names.** From Task 4.2, `formatCount(n)` and `countNoun(n, one, other)` live in `@protspace/utils` (`packages/utils/src/count-text.ts`), imported by core and the app alike; core's `src/utils/count-text.ts` is deleted in that commit. Every new string names an annotation by `annotationLabel(key, definition)` and pluralises through `countNoun`. The plot's count noun is "proteins".
- **Search.** Single-hit zoom: `k = max(current k, 8)`, clamped to `zoomExtent` `[0.1, 1000]`, the protein at the plot centre, untweened. "Zoom to them": the selected proteins' bounding box fitted inside the 40 px fit margins, untweened; a single point uses the single-hit rule. A paste never zooms. The report lists at most 50 missing IDs, then "and {formatCount(n)} more"; "Copy missing IDs" copies all of them, one per line.
- **Filter.** The live count keeps the builder's 300 ms debounce and runs only while the Filter panel shows. Structural reasons are computed at once; count-based ones wait for the count (Apply disabled, no reason text, while counting).
- **Structure picker.** At most 50 menu items (`MAX_STRUCTURE_CHOICES`), in selection order, always including the shown protein; searchable above 8; items render only while the menu is open.

## Review Focus

1. **One Escape press doing two things, or nothing.** Escape with a typed query in the search box, a hovered or focused `ps-tooltip`, the projection details pinned, an EAT click (connectors drawn and a protein selected), the figure editor open with an overlay selected, or a menu open over a dialog: each press must undo exactly one step, top first, and with nothing open must reach the connectors, then the selection, then the tool. Moving the fallbacks to the bubble phase only helps owners that `preventDefault`. Pinned by Task 4.1 (`layers.test.ts` bubble and `defaultPrevented` cases; `dropdown-helpers.test.ts`: a press a shown tooltip already took does not also empty the search box; `workbench-escape.spec.ts`: EAT click → connectors → selection → Move; details panel; editor never clears the selection) and Task 4.14 (editor: deselect, then close).
2. **Undo inside text fields and at 573K.** ⌘Z/Ctrl+Z in the search box, a filter value field (inside two shadow roots) or a figure editor input must edit the text, not the selection; undoing a lasso of hundreds of thousands of ids must not copy arrays, and a long session must not hold more than 2M ids. Pinned by Task 4.6 (`undo-controller.test.ts` with editable targets inside shadow-root paths and an open dialog; `undo-history.test.ts` caps by reference; `workbench-undo.spec.ts` Ctrl+Z in the search box).
3. **A filter draft racing the EAT slider and the count.** A dirty draft, then a slider move, then Apply; Cancel after a slider move; switching Legend ↔ Filter mid-edit; Apply's reason flashing a stale number during the 300 ms count; the panel switch resizing the plot. Pinned by Task 4.4 (`query-apply-state.test.ts`: structural reasons win over `counting`) and Task 4.5 (controller tests for the slider against clean and dirty drafts, the draft's condition id kept; e2e: no plot resize on switch, EAT draft mirror).
4. **A pasted list of thousands of IDs.** 10K tokens, most missing, mixed case, separated by commas, semicolons and newlines, some already selected, some hidden by the filter: the page must stay responsive (no 573K-entry map built per paste, at most 50 missing IDs rendered), the report must say what happened, and a single hidden hit must not zoom to nothing. Pinned by Task 4.7 (`resolve-ids.test.ts` cache by array identity; component tests for the cap and "and N more"; controller test that a false `zoomToProteins` reports "hidden in this view").
5. **A destructive step whose way back is unreachable.** Clearing stored data (OPFS, irreversible) without confirmation, by "Clear stored data" or by "Load default", which deletes it too; an Undo toast raised while the figure editor's modal dialog is open (hidden and inert under the top layer); a stale Undo toast undoing a newer step; the last imported file vanishing when the user tries an example. Pinned by Task 4.8 (confirm before either banner button deletes the copy, in `startup.test.ts`, `workbench-feedback.spec.ts` and `dataset-recovery.spec.ts`; a stale toast is dismissed when the history top changes, and its watcher goes when the toast closes), Task 4.14 (Undo strip inside the dialog) and Task 4.10 (the last file survives a menu example and reopens).

## Rulings

Escape, selection, status and undo (R1):

- Fallbacks run in a window bubble-phase listener, skipped when `defaultPrevented`; layers stay in capture (R1 §3). Keeping capture and turning every component Escape into a layer was rejected: the search's "typed query, list not open" case is not a layer.
- The duplicate-stack spider is a layer pushed by the plot while expanded; returning the tool to Move is `ESCAPE_ORDER.tool = 30`, after the selection (R1 Q2).
- A shown `ps-tooltip` calls `preventDefault` when Escape hides it, so hiding a tooltip is that press's one step (decision 11's "each press undoes one step"; WCAG 1.4.13 is kept).
- The figure editor gets a minimal layer in 4.1 so the order is right from the first task; 4.14 replaces it with `ps-dialog` (R1 Q9).
- The selection bar and the status corner are core Lit elements (`protspace-selection-bar`, `protspace-plot-status`) in `components/plot-tools/`, wired by the runtime, never React state: no status-store churn at brush rate, `PlotArea` stays memoised, embedders get them (R1 §3).
- "Show only" in the undo set and in the chip means plot isolation (the bar's "Show only these"); the chip reads "Showing only 1,204 proteins · 2 steps". Design 13's example "Showing only 3 categories · 2 steps" names a noun the isolation cannot report (it keeps proteins, not categories); the decision itself (a chip per narrowing, with its step count and an ✕) is kept. Legend hiding is the separate "4 categories hidden" chip and is not undoable (R1 Q1).
- A brush or lasso **start** ends a pinned tooltip, so a pin never floats over a lasso path (R1 Q3).
- Chip copy follows the design ("Filtered · 2 conditions"), plural-aware, in the mockup's chip style (R1 Q4).
- The count leaves the plot in the app: the scatterplot gains `hide-status` and `view-status-change`; embedders keep `.plot-indicator`; its noun becomes "proteins" in both places (R1 Q7, R5 Q3).
- The isolation chip has no "open" action (no panel edits an isolation); its ✕ resets every step. The filter chip opens the Filter panel; the hidden chip opens the Legend panel.
- Design 13 says the history "lives in the interaction controller and holds protein-id sets, not plot state": the history instance is created and owned by the interaction controller (`interactionController.history`); the selection and filter controllers record and apply their own entries; `undo-controller.ts` owns only the keys and routing (R1 §3 placement, adjusted to the design). Filter entries hold the applied matched-id set together with the query that produced it, and undo writes that id set back to the plot's filter channel without re-evaluating (design: id sets; R2 §5: the query keeps the chip count and the draft right).
- The EAT reliability slider is not recorded (R1 Q5, R2 Q6). Ctrl+Z works while a non-modal popover or menu is open; it is blocked in text fields and modal dialogs (R1 Q6). Caps: 100 steps or 2M ids (R1 Q8).
- Clear and Isolate leave the plot tools in 4.2; Reset stays there (renamed group "Isolation") for one task and leaves in 4.3 when the chip's ✕ replaces it, so no task leaves isolation without a way out.
- `formatCount`/`countNoun` move to `@protspace/utils` in 4.2, the first task whose app code needs them (phase 3 ruling: "4.11 may move them"); the shell must not import core values on the first-paint path.

Filter (R2):

- Apply keeps the panel open; the draft becomes clean and Apply then reads "No changes to apply" (R2 Q1). Cancel reverts the draft to the applied filter and keeps the panel open; it is disabled while the draft is clean; the header's ✕ closes the panel (Q2).
- An empty or match-all draft cannot be applied; Reset and the chip's ✕ remove a filter (Q3). Reset clears the applied filter and the draft, is recorded for undo, and keeps the label "Reset" (Q4).
- External changes against a dirty draft: the slider replaces only its column's condition (keeping the draft's condition id); the chip ✕ and Undo keep the dirty draft's other edits; a new dataset discards everything (Q5).
- Rail: Legend, Structure, Filter in that order; clicking the active panel's item collapses the sidebar; the view bar's Filter button never collapses, it opens the panel and focuses its heading (Q7). The Filter rail item shows `.wb-rail-dot` while a filter is applied (Q9).
- Reasons number the flat leaf conditions 1-based in display order, and each row shows its number (Q8).
- The query modules move to `components/query-builder/` in a move-only commit first; the shared `annotation-name.ts` and `annotation-categories.ts` move to `components/common/` in the same commit (R5 Q6), so the later picker move (4.16) imports them from there.
- The count stays in the builder (300 ms debounce, only while the panel shows); no Web Worker (the snapshot is not transferable without copying 573K rows).
- `panel: 'legend' | 'filter'` joins `LayoutState` with default `'legend'`; the v1 key stays (a missing field takes its default). The filter itself is not persisted.

Search, notifications, loading (R3):

- Enter on a typed ID and a suggestion pick both zoom (one protein added); a paste never zooms (R3 Q1). Single-hit zoom `k = max(current k, 8)`, untweened (Q2).
- A found protein hidden by the filter, isolation or a hidden category is selected anyway; the zoom is skipped and the report says "{id} is selected but hidden in this view" (Q3).
- The paste report lives in the search's own popup (a layer), not a toast (Q4).
- Toasts: bottom-centre of the plot, lifted above the selection bar, at most 360 px wide (Q5). Undo for Reset filters and the chip ✕ is the history step itself; the toast is a shortcut to it, and a stale toast (the history top changed) is dismissed (Q7).
- New figure's and Reset's Undo live inside the figure editor (Q6, R4 Q6); 4.14 owns them, 4.8 owns only the app's notification module.
- The scatterplot's drag handlers and `file-dropped` go (design: "Drop handling moves to the shell"); the shell re-dispatches `file-dropped` on `#myDataLoader`, so the event name survives (Q8, **BREAKING** for embedders, documented).
- The overlay keeps its positional `update()` signature; only its DOM and copy change (Q9). It builds no `innerHTML`.
- The recovery banner keeps `role="alert"` (no `aria-live`), mounts inside the plot area, and never takes focus; it is not a dialog, since the plot stays usable through Import (Q10).
- `datasetPhase` in the status store gates the empty state; it starts `'starting'`, so "Drop a file…" never flashes before startup resolves. While `'loading'` the workbench root is `inert`, so Tab cannot reach the bars behind the overlay.
- A dedicated workbench `<Toaster id="workbench">` renders in `.wb-body`; the App-level toaster stays for the other routes; `setNotifyTarget('workbench')` runs on mount and `setNotifyTarget(null)` in the effect cleanup.

Import, export, figure editor (R4):

- Close keeps the editor state (footer Close, the dialog's ✕, Escape); there is no discard button; Undo covers New figure and Reset (R4 Q1, design 15).
- A menu example no longer clears the stored import, so "Last file" stays useful (R4 Q2). This deviates from `openspec/specs/example-datasets/spec.md` ("Choosing an item SHALL … replace the user's stored import"); Task 8.3 writes the delta. The recovery banner's "Load default" and "Clear stored data" still clear it, and both now ask first (Task 4.8): either button deletes the only copy. Keeping the file on "Load default" was rejected, because startup retries a stored import whose last load failed, so the banner would come back on every visit until the user cleared it. The menu method is renamed to say what it does (`loadChosenExample`).
- The current example keeps its ⓘ inside the menu (shown disabled with a check); the app-bar name has none (R4 Q3; the spec's "the current-dataset name SHALL offer the same info control" delta goes to 8.3). The menu's "Current dataset" block goes, and `currentDatasetName` leaves the import menu's API.
- The Import panel is a `ps-popover` (`panel-role="dialog"`), not a `ps-menu`: each example has an interactive ⓘ, which cannot sit inside a `menuitem`. The Export menu is a `ps-menu` (plain actions and one checkbox).
- `protspace-info-popover` is rebuilt on `ps-popover` once for all its users (the annotation picker, the legend header, the EAT block, the score strips, the import menu, the projection details), so a bubble inside a top-layer panel is never clipped (phase 2 and 3 rulings deferred it here).
- Every export confirms: the utils exporter methods return the file name they wrote (null when there was nothing to export) and the IDs export uses a Blob URL instead of a `data:` URI.
- Restyle depth for the figure editor: tokens, the LEGACY removal, `ps-button` footer, `ps-tooltip` instead of its native `title` attributes; native inputs stay (R4 Q4). With a drawing tool active and nothing selected, Escape closes the editor (Q5). `currentProjection` is wired by the host (Q7).
- The figure editor's split (4.13) changes no behaviour and keeps one shadow root: sections are render modules with `renderX(model, handlers)`, and the inset capture cache is a class; tests that reached moved private members are renamed in the same commit, no forwarding methods.
- The editor's export failure shows inside the dialog (`showExportError`), because a toast would sit under the modal.

Structure and text (R5):

- After a multi-selection the structure shows a single added protein, else the shown protein while it is still selected, else the last (R5 Q1). The header list: first 50 in selection order plus the shown one, "First 50 of N selected", searchable above 8 (Q2).
- The resource links get their own row under the structure header that wraps instead of clipping, and the pinned tooltip lists them too (the only surface while the structure waits behind a collapsed sidebar). An overflow "⋯" menu was rejected (an extra click; the mockup shows all four).
- The figure's default legend title is the annotation's display name; a stored publish state keeps its own title (Q4).
- The annotation picker keeps its own listbox inside a `ps-popover` rather than `ps-menu`: its rows hold an eye toggle and an ⓘ (nested interactive), and `ps-menu`'s search matches badge text (Q5). It moves to `components/annotation-select/`.
- No per-annotation category counts in picker rows in this phase (Q7).

Plan review (two judges; applied unless noted):

- The task fragments are the contract: an implementer sees the header sections and its own task, and each task's Files and Interfaces blocks below were reconciled with the accepted interface change requests (`filter` icon in 4.3; `onExpandedChange` via an `expandedKey` accessor in 4.1; `focusChip` in 4.3; `query-reset` committing only when a filter was applied; `sameQuery` exported; `Rail` props; `applyFirstCategoryFilter` in the helpers; `bindImportMenu` returning `dispose`; the native Import trigger; the `secondary` Export trigger; `ps-menu` focusing only a checked radio; `LoadMeta.fileName`; `datasetPhaseFor`; `renderPresets`/`renderOptions`; the `InsetRenderCache` class; `annotationDefinitions` on the projection details).
- "Load default" on the recovery banner also deletes the stored import, so it asks first, like "Clear stored data" (Task 4.8). Keeping the file instead was rejected: startup retries a stored import whose last load failed, so the banner would return on every visit.
- `isModalOpen` keeps `protspace-publish-modal` permanently (the editor's `ps-dialog` sits in a shadow root `document.querySelector` cannot reach) and, from Task 4.12, also blocks undo while a dataset loads.
- `handleDropdownEscape` ignores a press already default-prevented (Task 4.1), so a shown tooltip and a typed search query never both react to one Escape.
- The query builder's `dirty` is `boolean | null` (null by default): an embedder that keeps no draft keeps today's Apply and Cancel (Task 4.4). Hiding the Filter panel closes any open picker through `closePopups()` (Task 4.5).
- Text glyphs and native `title` tooltips go from the modules this phase rebuilds: `external-link` lands in 4.9 (info popover "Learn more", then the import menu's "About these examples" and 4.15's links); the query builder and protein search drop their `title`s (4.4, 4.7).
- The disabled-control tooltips (locked width in 4.14, TED in 4.15) keep the control disabled and rely on pointer events reaching disabled controls in current Chromium and Firefox plus the tooltip's `aria-describedby`; browser tests pin it. A wrapper is the fallback for the width field only (the TED button must stay a direct child of its segmented control).
- Tasks 4.4 and 4.9–4.16 end with a full e2e run, as 4.1–4.3 and 4.5–4.8 already did.
- Task 4.12 is not split (judge B's optional m9): most of its code is given verbatim, and a split would renumber four tasks and their cross-references for margin alone.

Plan shape:

- Sixteen tasks, two more than the preferred fourteen: the five largest jobs (selection UI, filter, import/export, figure editor, text) each need two tasks to stay within one implementer's budget, and sixteen make four review blocks of four: 4.1–4.4, 4.5–4.8, 4.9–4.12, 4.13–4.16.
- `tasks.md` section 4 is rewritten to list this plan's sixteen tasks in the commit that adds the plan; the ticks land at the end of the phase.

### Task 4.1: The Escape order wired through the app

Escape takes one step per press through one order: the top layer, then the EAT connectors, then the selection, then the selection tool (decision 11). The layer stack's fallbacks move to the window's bubble phase so a component that handled the press keeps it, the scatterplot registers its connectors fallback, the selection controller registers the selection and tool fallbacks in place of its document listener, and the three remaining non-layer Escape owners (the duplicate-stack spider, the pinned projection details, the figure editor) become layers.

- [ ] **Step 3: Move the fallbacks to the bubble phase**

In `packages/core/src/components/kit/layers.ts`:

Replace the module doc comment (the first comment block, ending `closes nothing.`) with:

```ts
/**
 * One stack of open layers (popovers, menus, dialogs, sheets, the figure editor, pinned panels) for
 * the whole page (design decision 11). Escape closes only the top layer, in the window's capture
 * phase, before any component sees the key. With no layer open, Escape first reaches the page's own
 * handlers; a handler that acts on it calls `preventDefault()` (or stops it). Then, in the window's
 * bubble phase, the registered fallbacks run in ascending `ESCAPE_ORDER` (EAT connectors, the
 * selection, the selection tool), and the first that handles it wins. So each press takes exactly
 * one step. A press that starts and ends outside the top layer closes it, so a drag that ends
 * outside closes nothing.
 */
```

Replace `export const ESCAPE_ORDER = { connectors: 10, selection: 20 } as const;` with:

```ts
export const ESCAPE_ORDER = { connectors: 10, selection: 20, tool: 30 } as const;
```

Replace the whole `function onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void { … }` with two functions:

```ts
/** Capture phase: the top layer takes Escape before anything else hears it. */
function onLayerKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
  if (event.key !== 'Escape' || event.isComposing) return;
  const top = topLayer();
  if (!top) return;
  event.preventDefault();
  event.stopImmediatePropagation();
  top.close();
}

/** Bubble phase: no layer was open and no component handled the press. */
function onFallbackKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
  if (event.key !== 'Escape' || event.isComposing || event.defaultPrevented) return;
  if (topLayer()) return;
  for (const fallback of [...fallbacks]) {
    if (fallback.handle(event)) {
      event.preventDefault();
      return;
    }
  }
}
```

In `install()`, replace the comment and the keydown line

```ts
  // Capture on window runs before any component's own handler.
  window.addEventListener('keydown', onKeydown, true);
```

with

```ts
  // Capture on window runs before any component's own handler; the fallbacks wait for the bubble
  // phase, after every component had its chance to handle the press.
  window.addEventListener('keydown', onLayerKeydown, true);
  window.addEventListener('keydown', onFallbackKeydown);
```

Run: `pnpm --filter @protspace/core exec vitest --run --project unit src/components/kit/layers.test.ts`
Expected: PASS (every case, old and new).

```ts
  private _expandedKey: string | null = null;
  // Every expand and collapse path writes `expandedKey`; the setter tells the host when the spider
  // opens or closes.
  private get expandedKey(): string | null {
    return this._expandedKey;
  }
  private set expandedKey(key: string | null) {
    const wasOpen = this._expandedKey !== null;
    this._expandedKey = key;
    if (wasOpen !== (key !== null)) this.deps.onExpandedChange?.(key !== null);
  }
```

```ts
  /**
```

```ts
   * element so typing Backspace inside the label-text input still erases characters instead of
   * deleting the overlay. Escape is the layer's (`_onEscapeLayer`).

  private _onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
```

```ts
/**
 * A stand-in for the layer stack's Escape fallbacks: `press()` runs them as one Escape press does,
 * in ascending order, until one acts.
 */
function fakeEscape() {
  const handlers = new Map<number, (event: KeyboardEvent) => boolean>();
  const register = vi.fn((order: number, handle: (event: KeyboardEvent) => boolean) => {
    handlers.set(order, handle);
    return () => {
      handlers.delete(order);
    };
  });
  const press = (): boolean => {
    for (const order of [...handlers.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b)) {
      if (handlers.get(order)!(new Event('keydown') as KeyboardEvent)) return true;
    }
    return false;
  };
  return { register, press, handlers };
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: Write the end-to-end Escape order**

Create `apps/web/tests/workbench-escape.spec.ts`:

```ts
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { expect, test, type Page } from '@playwright/test';
import {
  chooseTool,
  dismissTourIfPresent,
  exportMenu,
  getSelectedProteinIds,
  openExplore,
  searchInput,
  selectAnnotation,
  viewBar,
  waitForProteinCount,
} from './helpers/explore';
import { STARTUP_URL_GLOB } from './helpers/fixtures';
import { stubStructureRequests } from './helpers/workbench';

const EAT_FIXTURE = fileURLToPath(
  new URL('./fixtures/phosphatase_eat.parquetbundle', import.meta.url),
);

const toolButton = (page: Page, name: string) =>
  page.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Plot tools' }).getByRole('button', { name, exact: true });

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  // A selection opens the structure viewer: answer its requests offline.
  await stubStructureRequests(page);
});

/** The EAT fixture, loaded through the data loader's file input as eat-visualization.spec.ts does. */
async function loadEatFixture(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.addInitScript(() => localStorage.setItem('driver.overviewTour', 'true'));
  await page.route(STARTUP_URL_GLOB, (route) => route.abort());
  await page.goto('/explore');
  await dismissTourIfPresent(page);
  await page.waitForFunction(() => {
    const loader = document.querySelector('protspace-data-loader') as
      | (Element & { loadFromFile?: unknown })
      | null;
    return typeof loader?.loadFromFile === 'function';
  });
  await page.locator('protspace-data-loader input[type="file"]').setInputFiles(EAT_FIXTURE);
  await waitForProteinCount(page, 832);
}

/** Clicks the first protein with an EAT transfer, as a point click reports it, and returns its id. */
function clickEatTransfer(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  return page.locator('#myPlot').evaluate((element) => {
    const plot = element as Element & {
      data: {
        protein_ids: string[];
        annotation_predicted?: Record<string, Array<unknown | null>>;
      };
    };
    const cells = plot.data.annotation_predicted?.ec ?? [];
    const index = cells.findIndex((cell) => cell !== null);
    if (index < 0) throw new Error('No EAT transfer was decoded');
    const proteinId = plot.data.protein_ids[index];
    element.dispatchEvent(
      new CustomEvent('protein-click', {
        detail: {
          proteinId,
          point: { originalIndex: index },
          modifierKeys: { ctrl: false, meta: false, shift: false, alt: false },
        },
        bubbles: true,
        composed: true,
      }),
    );
    return proteinId;
  });
}

/** Selects the dataset's first protein through the search box and returns its id. */
async function selectFirstBySearch(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  const id = await page
    .locator('#myPlot')
    .evaluate(
      (plot) => (plot as Element & { data: { protein_ids: string[] } }).data.protein_ids[0],
    );
  await searchInput(page).fill(id);
  await searchInput(page).press('Enter');
  await expect.poll(() => getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([id]);
  return id;
}

/** Two frames: a wrong clear shows at once in the search box and reaches the plot after the paint. */
const twoFrames = (page: Page) =>
  page.evaluate(
    () => new Promise((resolve) => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(resolve))),
  );

test.describe('the Escape order', () => {
  test('an EAT click: Escape 1 hides the connectors and keeps the selection, 2 clears the selection, 3 returns to Move', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await loadEatFixture(page);
    await selectAnnotation(page, 'ec');
    await chooseTool(page, 'Box select');
    const connectors = page.locator('#myPlot line.eat-provenance-connector');

    const target = await clickEatTransfer(page);
    await expect(connectors.first()).toBeAttached();
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([target]);

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(connectors).toHaveCount(0);
    await twoFrames(page);
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([target]);
    await expect(toolButton(page, 'Box select')).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect.poll(() => getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([]);
    await expect(toolButton(page, 'Box select')).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(toolButton(page, 'Move and zoom')).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true');
  });

  test('with the projection details pinned, Escape closes only them', async ({ page }) => {
    await openExplore(page);
    const id = await selectFirstBySearch(page);
    // Give the details something to show whatever the fixture's projection metadata holds.
    await page.locator('#myProjectionMetadata').evaluate((details: Element) => {
      (details as Element & { projection: unknown }).projection = {
        name: 'Fixture projection',
        metadata: { n_neighbors: 15, min_dist: 0.1, metric: 'cosine' },
      };
    });
    const trigger = viewBar(page).getByRole('button', { name: 'View projection metadata' });
    await trigger.click();
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();
    await twoFrames(page);
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([id]);

    // The details are closed: the next press reaches the selection.
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect.poll(() => getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test('Escape in the search box with a typed query empties the box and keeps the selection', async ({
    page,
  }) => {
    await openExplore(page);
    const id = await selectFirstBySearch(page);

    await searchInput(page).fill('zz-no-such-protein');
    await searchInput(page).press('Escape');
    await expect(searchInput(page)).toHaveValue('');
    await twoFrames(page);
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([id]);
  });

  test('in the figure editor, Escape never clears the plot’s selection', async ({ page }) => {
    await openExplore(page);
    const id = await selectFirstBySearch(page);
    await searchInput(page).blur();
    // The same handler the Export menu's Figure editor item reaches.
    await exportMenu(page).evaluate((menu) =>
      menu.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('open-publish-editor', { bubbles: true, composed: true })),
    );
    const editor = page.locator('protspace-publish-modal');
    await expect(editor).toBeAttached();
    // An overlay, selected, as a click on it in the editor leaves it.
    await editor.evaluate((modal) => {
      const m = modal as unknown as {
        _state: Record<string, unknown>;
        _selectedItem: unknown;
        requestUpdate(): void;
      };
      m._state = {
        ...m._state,
        overlays: [
          {
            type: 'circle',
            cx: 0.5,
            cy: 0.5,
            rx: 0.1,
            ry: 0.1,
            rotation: 0,
            color: '#000',
            strokeWidth: 2,
          },
        ],
      };
      m._selectedItem = { kind: 'overlay', index: 0 };
      m.requestUpdate();
    });
    const selectedItem = () =>
      editor.evaluate((modal) => (modal as unknown as { _selectedItem: unknown })._selectedItem);

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect.poll(selectedItem).toBeNull();
    await expect(editor).toBeAttached();
    await twoFrames(page);
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([id]);

    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
    await expect(editor).toHaveCount(0);
    await twoFrames(page);
    expect(await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([id]);
  });
});
```

```ts
  t.k * x + t.x,
  t.k * y + t.y,
];

    const t = zoomTransformFor([[100, 50]], VIEW)!;
    expect(t.k).toBe(8);
    expect(onScreen(t, [100, 50])).toEqual([200, 150]);
  });

  it('a current k above singleK is kept', () => {
    const t = zoomTransformFor([[100, 50]], { ...VIEW, currentK: 20 })!;
    expect(t.k).toBe(20);
    expect(onScreen(t, [100, 50])).toEqual([200, 150]);
  });

        [100, 50],
        [200, 100],
      ],
      VIEW,

    expect(t.k).toBeCloseTo(1.6);
    const [left, top] = onScreen(t, [0, 0]);
    const [right, bottom] = onScreen(t, [200, 100]);
    expect(left).toBeCloseTo(40);
    expect(right).toBeCloseTo(360);
    expect(top).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(40);
    expect(bottom).toBeLessThanOrEqual(260);
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The pure transform**

Create `packages/core/src/components/scatter-plot/interaction/zoom-to-points.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * The zoom transform that frames some points (design decision 15: "Zoom to them" and a single
 * search hit). Points are in the plot's screen pixels at k = 1, as its scales place them. One
 * point, or a box of no size, lands at the centre at `max(currentK, singleK)`, so a hit is never
 * shown smaller than the user had zoomed; several are fitted inside `margin` on every side. `k` is
 * clamped to `extent`, the plot's zoom limits. Null when there is nothing to frame.
 */
export function zoomTransformFor(
  points: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, number]>,
  view: {
    width: number;
    height: number;
    margin: number;
    currentK: number;
    extent: readonly [number, number];
    singleK: number;
  },
): { k: number; x: number; y: number } | null {
  if (points.length === 0) return null;
  let minX = Infinity;
  let minY = Infinity;
  let maxX = -Infinity;
  let maxY = -Infinity;
  for (const [x, y] of points) {
    if (x < minX) minX = x;
    if (x > maxX) maxX = x;
    if (y < minY) minY = y;
    if (y > maxY) maxY = y;
  }
  const boxWidth = maxX - minX;
  const boxHeight = maxY - minY;
  let k: number;
  if (boxWidth === 0 && boxHeight === 0) {
    k = Math.max(view.currentK, view.singleK);
  } else {
    const roomWidth = Math.max(1, view.width - 2 * view.margin);
    const roomHeight = Math.max(1, view.height - 2 * view.margin);
    k = Math.min(
      boxWidth > 0 ? roomWidth / boxWidth : Infinity,
      boxHeight > 0 ? roomHeight / boxHeight : Infinity,
    );
  }
  const [low, high] = view.extent;
  k = Math.min(high, Math.max(low, k));
  return {
    k,
    x: view.width / 2 - k * ((minX + maxX) / 2),
    y: view.height / 2 - k * ((minY + maxY) / 2),
  };
}
```

```ts
    projections: [{ name: 'umap', dimension: 2, data: new Float32Array([0, 0, 5, 5, 10, 10]) }],
    annotations: {
      fam: { kind: 'categorical', values: ['A'], colors: ['#336699'], shapes: ['circle'] },
    },
    annotation_data: { fam: new Int32Array(3) },
  } as unknown as VisualizationData;
}

async function mountPlot(): Promise<ProtspaceScatterplot> {
  const plot = document.createElement('protspace-scatterplot');
  plot.style.cssText = 'display: block; width: 480px; height: 360px';
  plot.selectedAnnotation = 'fam';
  plot.data = makeData();
  document.body.append(plot);
  await plot.updateComplete;
  await vi.waitFor(() => {
    const rect = plot.getBoundingClientRect();
    const p = plot.getProteinClientPosition('P3')!;
    expect(plot.pickInteractivePointAt(p.x - rect.left, p.y - rect.top)).not.toBeNull();
  });
  return plot;
}

const transformOf = (plot: ProtspaceScatterplot) =>
  (plot as unknown as { _transform: { k: number; x: number; y: number } })._transform;
const svgRect = (plot: ProtspaceScatterplot) =>
  plot.shadowRoot!.querySelector('svg')!.getBoundingClientRect();

describe('scatterplot zoomToProteins', () => {
  it('one id moves that point to the plot centre ±1 px at k ≥ 8', async () => {
    const plot = await mountPlot();
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins(['P2'])).toBe(true);
    const rect = svgRect(plot);
    const p = plot.getProteinClientPosition('P2')!;
    expect(Math.abs(p.x - (rect.left + rect.width / 2))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(Math.abs(p.y - (rect.top + rect.height / 2))).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(transformOf(plot).k).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(8);
  });

  it('several ids fit their box inside 40 px', async () => {
    const plot = await mountPlot();
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins(['P1', 'P3'])).toBe(true);
    const rect = svgRect(plot);
    const p1 = plot.getProteinClientPosition('P1')!;
    const p3 = plot.getProteinClientPosition('P3')!;
    for (const p of [p1, p3]) {
      expect(p.x).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(rect.left + 39);
      expect(p.x).toBeLessThanOrEqual(rect.right - 39);
      expect(p.y).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(rect.top + 39);
      expect(p.y).toBeLessThanOrEqual(rect.bottom - 39);
    }
    // The box fills the room on its tighter side.
    const fill = Math.max(
      Math.abs(p3.x - p1.x) / (rect.width - 80),
      Math.abs(p3.y - p1.y) / (rect.height - 80),
    );
    expect(fill).toBeCloseTo(1, 1);
  });

  it('unknown or unplotted ids return false and leave the transform', async () => {
    const plot = await mountPlot();
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins([])).toBe(false);
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins(['nope'])).toBe(false);
    plot.filteredProteinIds = ['P1', 'P3'];
    plot.filtersActive = true;
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(plot.getProteinClientPosition('P2')).toBeNull());
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins(['P2'])).toBe(false);
    expect(plot.zoomToProteins(['P2', 'nope'])).toBe(false);
    expect(transformOf(plot)).toMatchObject({ k: 1, x: 0, y: 0 });
  });

  it('a wheel after zoomToProteins starts from the new transform (d3 state in sync)', async () => {
    const plot = await mountPlot();
    plot.zoomToProteins(['P2']);
    const before = transformOf(plot).k;
    const p = plot.getProteinClientPosition('P2')!;
    plot.shadowRoot!.querySelector('svg')!.dispatchEvent(
      new WheelEvent('wheel', {
        clientX: p.x,
        clientY: p.y,
        deltaY: -100,
        bubbles: true,
        cancelable: true,
      }),
    );
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(transformOf(plot).k).toBeGreaterThan(before));
    // One wheel step from 8×, not from the 1× d3 would still hold had the zoom bypassed it.
    expect(transformOf(plot).k).toBeLessThan(before * 1.5);
  });
});
```

```ts
  /**
   * Pans and zooms, untweened, to frame the plotted, visible proteins among `ids`: one lands at
   * the plot centre at 8× or more, several are fitted inside a 40 px margin. Returns false and
   * leaves the view alone when none of them is plotted and visible (unknown, filtered out,
   * isolated away or hidden by the legend).
   */
  zoomToProteins(ids: readonly string[]): boolean {
    const scales = this._scales;
    const plotData = this._plotData;
    if (!scales || !this._interaction || plotData.length === 0 || ids.length === 0) return false;
    const { visible } = this._style.interactable(plotData);
    const originalIndices = plotData.originalIndices;
    let found = 0;
    let minX = Infinity;
    let minY = Infinity;
    let maxX = -Infinity;
    let maxY = -Infinity;
    const include = (slot: number) => {
      if (slot < 0 || slot >= plotData.length || visible[slot] !== 1) return;
      const x = scales.x(plotData.xs[slot]);
      const y = scales.y(plotData.ys[slot]);
      found++;
      if (x < minX) minX = x;
      if (x > maxX) maxX = x;
      if (y < minY) minY = y;
      if (y > maxY) maxY = y;
    };
    if (ids.length === 1) {
      // A search hit: one indexOf, never a set over every plotted protein.
      const proteinIndex = plotData.proteinIds.indexOf(ids[0]);
      if (proteinIndex >= 0) {
        include(originalIndices ? originalIndices.indexOf(proteinIndex) : proteinIndex);
      }
    } else {
      const wanted = new Set(ids);
      for (let slot = 0; slot < plotData.length; slot++) {
        if (visible[slot] !== 1) continue;
        const id = plotData.proteinIds[originalIndices ? originalIndices[slot] : slot];
        if (wanted.has(id)) include(slot);
      }
    }
    if (found === 0) return false;
    const { width, height, zoomExtent } = this._mergedConfig;
    // The box's two corners stand for every point in it.
    const t = zoomTransformFor(
      [
        [minX, minY],
        [maxX, maxY],
      ],
      { width, height, margin: 40, currentK: this._transform.k, extent: zoomExtent, singleK: 8 },
    );
    if (!t) return false;
    this._interaction.setTransform(d3.zoomIdentity.translate(t.x, t.y).scale(t.k));
    return true;
  }
```

Create `packages/core/src/components/plot-tools/selection-bar.ts`:

```ts
import { LitElement, html, type PropertyValues } from 'lit';
import { property, state } from 'lit/decorators.js';
import { countNoun } from '@protspace/utils';
import { customElement } from '../../utils/safe-custom-element';
import '../kit/button';
import type { PsButton } from '../kit/button';
import { selectionBarStyles } from './selection-bar.styles';

type SelectionAction = 'isolate' | 'zoom' | 'copy' | 'clear';

const ACTIONS: ReadonlyArray<{ action: SelectionAction; label: string; event: string }> = [
  { action: 'isolate', label: 'Show only these', event: 'isolate-data' },
  { action: 'zoom', label: 'Zoom to them', event: 'zoom-to-selection' },
  { action: 'copy', label: 'Copy IDs', event: 'copy-selection' },
  { action: 'clear', label: 'Clear', event: 'clear-selections' },
];

/**
 * The selection's actions at the bottom of the plot, shown while proteins are selected (design
 * decision 13): the count, then Show only these, Zoom to them, Copy IDs and Clear. A toolbar with
 * one Tab stop; the arrow keys move between its buttons. It reports presses; the host's selection
 * controller acts and sets `selectedCount`.
 *
 * @fires isolate-data - `{}`
 * @fires zoom-to-selection - `{}`
 * @fires copy-selection - `{}`
 * @fires clear-selections - `{}`
 */
@customElement('protspace-selection-bar')
export class ProtspaceSelectionBar extends LitElement {
  static styles = selectionBarStyles;

  @property({ type: Number, attribute: 'selected-count' }) selectedCount = 0;
  /** Show only these is off: the view holds too few points to isolate from. */
  @property({ type: Boolean, attribute: 'can-isolate' }) canIsolate = true;
  /**
   * Called after Clear or Show only these hid the bar while it held focus, so focus lands on
   * something useful instead of the page body.
   */
  @property({ attribute: false }) returnFocus: ((action: 'clear' | 'isolate') => void) | null =
    null;

  /** The toolbar's one Tab stop: the button focused last. */
  @state() private _tabStop: SelectionAction = 'isolate';

  protected willUpdate(changed: PropertyValues<this>): void {
    if (changed.has('selectedCount')) this.hidden = this.selectedCount === 0;
  }

  render() {
    const enabled = ACTIONS.filter(({ action }) => this._isEnabled(action));
    const stop = enabled.some(({ action }) => action === this._tabStop)
      ? this._tabStop
      : enabled[0]?.action;
    return html`<div
      class="bar"
      role="toolbar"
      aria-label="Selection"
      @keydown=${this._onKeydown}
      @focusin=${this._onFocusIn}
    >
      <span class="selection-count" aria-live="polite"
        >${countNoun(this.selectedCount, 'protein', 'proteins')} selected</span
      >
      ${ACTIONS.map(
        ({ action, label }) =>
          html`<ps-button
            size="sm"
            variant="ghost"
            data-action=${action}
            tabindex=${action === stop ? '0' : '-1'}
            ?disabled=${!this._isEnabled(action)}
            @click=${() => this._press(action)}
            >${label}</ps-button
          >`,
      )}
    </div>`;
  }

  private _isEnabled(action: SelectionAction): boolean {
    return action !== 'isolate' || this.canIsolate;
  }

  private async _press(action: SelectionAction): Promise<void> {
    const hadFocus = this.shadowRoot!.activeElement !== null;
    const { event } = ACTIONS.find((entry) => entry.action === action)!;
    this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(event, { detail: {}, bubbles: true, composed: true }));
    if (!hadFocus || (action !== 'clear' && action !== 'isolate')) return;
    // The host empties the selection while the event runs; the bar hides in the next update.
    await this.updateComplete;
    if (this.hidden) this.returnFocus?.(action);
  }

  private _onFocusIn = (event: FocusEvent) => {
    const action = (event.target as HTMLElement).dataset?.action as SelectionAction | undefined;
    if (action) this._tabStop = action;
  };

  /** The toolbar pattern: ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (and Home, End) move between enabled buttons. */
  private _onKeydown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
    const { key } = event;
    if (key !== 'ArrowRight' && key !== 'ArrowLeft' && key !== 'Home' && key !== 'End') return;
    const enabled = [...this.renderRoot.querySelectorAll<PsButton>('ps-button')].filter(
      (b) => !b.disabled,
    );
    const current = enabled.indexOf(this.shadowRoot!.activeElement as PsButton);
    if (current === -1) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    const last = enabled.length - 1;
    const next =
      key === 'Home'
        ? 0
        : key === 'End'
          ? last
          : key === 'ArrowRight'
            ? (current + 1) % enabled.length
            : (current + last) % enabled.length;
    enabled[next].focus();
  };
}

declare global {
  interface HTMLElementTagNameMap {
    'protspace-selection-bar': ProtspaceSelectionBar;
  }
}
```

```ts
  /** Set when Reset had focus: leaving isolation removes it. */
  private restoreFocus = false;

  private resetIsolation = () => {
    this.restoreFocus = this.shadowRoot!.activeElement !== null;
    this.emit('reset-isolation');
  };

  protected updated(): void {
    if (!this.restoreFocus) return;
    this.restoreFocus = false;
    // Reset is still there.
    if (this.shadowRoot!.activeElement) return;
    this.focusTool();
  }

  /** Focuses the tool strip's one Tab stop: the current tool, or Move and zoom. */
  focusTool(): void {
    const tools = this.renderRoot.querySelectorAll<PsIconButton>('.tools ps-icon-button');
    tools[TOOLS.findIndex(({ tool }) => tool === this.tabStop)]?.focus();
  }
```

```ts
  const onZoomToSelection = () => {
    // Zoom to what the bar counts: land a search pick still waiting first.
    commit.flush();
    plotElement.zoomToProteins(selected);
  };

  const onCopySelection = () => {
    const ids = selected;
    if (ids.length === 0) return;
    // Through a promise: in a page that is not a secure context `navigator.clipboard` is missing.
    void Promise.resolve()
      .then(() => navigator.clipboard.writeText(ids.join('\n')))
      .then(
        () => notify.success(getSelectionCopiedNotification(ids.length)),
        () => notify.error(getSelectionCopyFailedNotification()),
      );
  };
```

```ts
/** The selection bar at the bottom of the plot; it shows while proteins are selected. */
export const selectionBar = (page: Page): Locator =>
  page.getByRole('toolbar', { name: 'Selection', exact: true });

/** One of the selection bar's actions. */
export const selectionBarAction = (
  page: Page,
  name: 'Show only these' | 'Zoom to them' | 'Copy IDs' | 'Clear',
): Locator => selectionBar(page).getByRole('button', { name, exact: true });

/** Reset, beside the plot's tool strip while the plot is isolated. */
const isolationReset = (page: Page): Locator =>
  page
    .getByRole('group', { name: 'Isolation', exact: true })
    .getByRole('button', { name: 'Reset', exact: true });
```

and replace the three action helpers' bodies:

```ts
/** Clears the selection with the bar's Clear and waits until the plot holds none; a no-op with none. */
export async function clearSelection(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  if ((await getSelectedProteinIds(page)).length === 0) return;
  await selectionBarAction(page, 'Clear').click();
  await expect.poll(() => getSelectedProteinIds(page)).toEqual([]);
}

/** Isolates the selected proteins with Show only these and waits until the plot is isolated. */
export async function isolateSelection(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await selectionBarAction(page, 'Show only these').click();
  await expect.poll(() => isIsolated(page)).toBe(true);
}

/** Leaves isolation with Reset and waits until the plot shows the full dataset again. */
export async function resetIsolation(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await isolationReset(page).click();
  await expect.poll(() => isIsolated(page)).toBe(false);
}
```

4. Replace the `### Plot Tools` section (its intro, both tables and the paragraph after them) with:

```md
### Plot Tools

The plot's tool strip, and beside it, while the plot is isolated, Reset.

| Property            | Type                              | Description                                 |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `tool`              | `'pan' \| 'rectangle' \| 'lasso'` | Pressed tool (`PlotTool`)                   |
| `selectionDisabled` | `boolean`                         | Box and Lasso are off; `selection-disabled` |
| `isolated`          | `boolean`                         | Reset shows while true                      |

| Event              | Detail     | Description             |
| ------------------ | ---------- | ----------------------- |
| `plot-tool-change` | `{ tool }` | A tool was chosen       |
| `fit-view`         | `{}`       | Fit to view was pressed |
| `reset-isolation`  | `{}`       | Reset was pressed       |

`focusTool()` focuses the strip's one Tab stop (the current tool). On the scatterplot, `pan` is
`selectionMode = false`; `rectangle` and `lasso` are `selectionMode = true` with that
`selectionTool`. `fit-view` maps to `resetZoom()`.

**BREAKING:** `selectedCount` (`selected-count`), Clear and Isolate, and their `clear-selections`
and `isolate-data` events moved to the selection bar.

### Selection Bar

`<protspace-selection-bar>` shows at the bottom-centre of its positioned parent while proteins are
selected: the count, then Show only these, Zoom to them, Copy IDs and Clear, in a toolbar named
"Selection" with one Tab stop (the arrow keys move between the buttons). It hides itself at 0 and
reports presses; the host acts and sets `selectedCount`.

| Property        | Type                                              | Description                                                                          |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `selectedCount` | `number`                                          | How many proteins are selected; `selected-count`                                     |
| `canIsolate`    | `boolean`                                         | Show only these is enabled (default `true`); `can-isolate`                           |
| `returnFocus`   | `((action: 'clear' \| 'isolate') => void) \| null` | Called when Clear or Show only these hid the bar while it held focus; JavaScript only |

| Event               | Detail | Description                |
| ------------------- | ------ | -------------------------- |
| `isolate-data`      | `{}`   | Show only these was pressed |
| `zoom-to-selection` | `{}`   | Zoom to them was pressed   |
| `copy-selection`    | `{}`   | Copy IDs was pressed       |
| `clear-selections`  | `{}`   | Clear was pressed          |
```

```ts
import { afterEach, beforeAll, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
import { page, userEvent } from 'vitest/browser';
import { adoptTheme } from '../kit/adopt-theme';
import type { PsIconButton } from '../kit/button';
import { deepActiveElement } from '../kit/focus';
import type { ProtspacePlotStatus, StatusChipKind } from './plot-status';
import './plot-status';

beforeAll(() => adoptTheme());
afterEach(() => document.body.replaceChildren());

async function mount(
  props: Partial<
    Pick<
      ProtspacePlotStatus,
      'count' | 'zoomedIn' | 'filterConditions' | 'isolation' | 'hiddenCategories'
    >
  > = {},
  parent: HTMLElement = document.body,
): Promise<ProtspacePlotStatus> {
  const el = document.createElement('protspace-plot-status');
  Object.assign(el, { count: 7831, ...props });
  parent.append(el);
  await el.updateComplete;
  await Promise.all([...el.shadowRoot!.querySelectorAll<PsIconButton>('ps-icon-button')].map((b) => b.updateComplete));
  return el;
}
const countText = (el: ProtspacePlotStatus) =>
  el.shadowRoot!.querySelector('.status-count')?.textContent?.trim() ?? null;
const chips = (el: ProtspacePlotStatus) => [
  ...el.shadowRoot!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.status-chip'),
];
const chipText = (chip: Element) =>
  chip.querySelector('.status-chip-open, .status-chip-text')!.textContent!.trim();
const clearButton = (el: ProtspacePlotStatus, kind: StatusChipKind) =>
  el.shadowRoot!.querySelector<PsIconButton>(`.status-chip[data-kind="${kind}"] ps-icon-button`)!;
const openButton = (el: ProtspacePlotStatus, kind: StatusChipKind) =>
  el.shadowRoot!.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(
    `.status-chip[data-kind="${kind}"] .status-chip-open`,
  );
const inner = (b: Element) => b.shadowRoot!.querySelector('button')!;
/** Every chip set, then cleared by its own ✕ as the host would. */
function clearsItself(el: ProtspacePlotStatus): void {
  el.addEventListener('status-clear', (event) => {
    const { kind } = (event as CustomEvent<{ kind: StatusChipKind }>).detail;
    if (kind === 'filter') el.filterConditions = 0;
    if (kind === 'isolation') el.isolation = null;
    if (kind === 'hidden') el.hiddenCategories = 0;
  });
}

describe('protspace-plot-status', () => {
  it('count text groups and pluralises; Zoomed in appended', async () => {
    const el = await mount({ count: 7831 });
    expect(countText(el)).toBe('7,831 proteins');
    el.zoomedIn = true;
    await el.updateComplete;
    expect(countText(el)).toBe('7,831 proteins · Zoomed in');
    el.count = 1;
    await el.updateComplete;
    expect(countText(el)).toBe('1 protein · Zoomed in');
  });

  it('null count hides it', async () => {
    const el = await mount({ count: null });
    expect(countText(el)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("each chip's text per the copy table, plural-aware (1 condition, 1 step, 1 category)", async () => {
    const el = await mount({
      filterConditions: 1,
      isolation: { steps: 1, size: 1 },
      hiddenCategories: 1,
    });
    expect(chips(el).map(chipText)).toEqual([
      'Filtered · 1 condition',
      'Showing only 1 protein · 1 step',
      '1 category hidden',
    ]);
    Object.assign(el, {
      filterConditions: 2,
      isolation: { steps: 2, size: 1204 },
      hiddenCategories: 4,
    });
    await el.updateComplete;
    expect(chips(el).map(chipText)).toEqual([
      'Filtered · 2 conditions',
      'Showing only 1,204 proteins · 2 steps',
      '4 categories hidden',
    ]);
  });

  it('chips render in the order filter, isolation, hidden', async () => {
    const el = await mount({ hiddenCategories: 3, filterConditions: 1 });
    expect(chips(el).map((chip) => chip.dataset.kind)).toEqual(['filter', 'hidden']);
    el.isolation = { steps: 1, size: 9 };
    await el.updateComplete;
    expect(chips(el).map((chip) => chip.dataset.kind)).toEqual(['filter', 'isolation', 'hidden']);
  });

  it('each ✕ has its own accessible name and fires status-clear with its kind', async () => {
    const el = await mount({
      filterConditions: 1,
      isolation: { steps: 1, size: 5 },
      hiddenCategories: 2,
    });
    for (const name of ['Remove filter', 'Show all proteins', 'Show hidden categories']) {
      await expect.element(page.getByRole('button', { name, exact: true })).toBeInTheDocument();
    }
    const kinds: string[] = [];
    // On the element, not document.body: the body's listeners would outlive this test.
    el.addEventListener('status-clear', (event) =>
      kinds.push((event as CustomEvent<{ kind: string }>).detail.kind),
    );
    for (const kind of ['filter', 'isolation', 'hidden'] as const) {
      inner(clearButton(el, kind)).click();
    }
    expect(kinds).toEqual(['filter', 'isolation', 'hidden']);
  });

  it('the filter and hidden chip bodies fire status-open; the isolation chip has no open control', async () => {
    const el = await mount({
      filterConditions: 1,
      isolation: { steps: 1, size: 5 },
      hiddenCategories: 2,
    });
    const kinds: string[] = [];
    el.addEventListener('status-open', (event) =>
      kinds.push((event as CustomEvent<{ kind: string }>).detail.kind),
    );
    openButton(el, 'filter')!.click();
    openButton(el, 'hidden')!.click();
    expect(kinds).toEqual(['filter', 'hidden']);
    expect(openButton(el, 'isolation')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('removing a focused chip moves focus to the next chip, else the count', async () => {
    const el = await mount({
      filterConditions: 1,
      isolation: { steps: 1, size: 5 },
      hiddenCategories: 2,
    });
    clearsItself(el);

    inner(clearButton(el, 'filter')).focus();
    await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}');
    // The isolation chip's first control is its ✕.
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(deepActiveElement()).toBe(inner(clearButton(el, 'isolation'))));

    await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}');
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(deepActiveElement()).toBe(openButton(el, 'hidden')));

    inner(clearButton(el, 'hidden')).focus();
    await userEvent.keyboard('{Enter}');
    await vi.waitFor(() =>
      expect(deepActiveElement()).toBe(el.shadowRoot!.querySelector('.status-count')),
    );
  });

  it('the count is role=status', async () => {
    await mount({ count: 42 });
    await expect.element(page.getByRole('status')).toHaveTextContent('42 proteins');
  });

  it('focusChip focuses a chip set in the same task, after its update', async () => {
    const el = await mount();
    expect(el.focusChip('isolation')).toBe(false);
    el.isolation = { steps: 1, size: 3 };
    expect(el.focusChip('isolation')).toBe(true);
    await vi.waitFor(() => expect(deepActiveElement()).toBe(inner(clearButton(el, 'isolation'))));
  });

  it('sits in the bottom-left corner; chips are 24 px tall', async () => {
    const parent = document.createElement('div');
    parent.style.cssText = 'position: relative; width: 800px; height: 400px';
    document.body.append(parent);
    const el = await mount({ filterConditions: 1 }, parent);
    const box = parent.getBoundingClientRect();
    const host = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    expect(Math.abs(host.left - box.left - 12)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(Math.abs(box.bottom - host.bottom - 12)).toBeLessThanOrEqual(1);
    expect(Math.round(chips(el)[0].getBoundingClientRect().height)).toBe(24);
  });
});
```
